prediction.whatIsNeededForEstimate: To compute an actual dollar range, the record needs: (1) the square footage of Shaw's condo unit, so the stated $275/sq ft rate can be turned into a total value; (2) the actual price Mostafavi paid A&M in the August 2015 sale (or a contemporaneous appraisal), to establish a 2015 baseline value; (3) a current appraisal or comparable sale supporting the $275/sq ft figure and its valuation date; and (4) any evidence of what Shaw would have needed to pay to exercise the ROFR (financing terms, closing costs) so the 'lost bargain' -- offer price versus fair value -- can be isolated rather than assuming pure appreciation is the measure.
prediction.likelyOutcome: On liability, Shaw should prevail: A&M's admitted failure to honor a clear, unambiguous ROFR term is a straightforward breach, and the ten-year Iowa limitations period for written contracts means the seven-year gap is not an absolute bar. The real fight -- and a genuinely close one for a bench trial -- is whether Shaw's post-breach conduct (continued payments, renegotiating a new ROFR with the successor owner, repeated purchase requests that never invoked the original breach) constitutes waiver, and whether his delay compresses the damages valuation window under a mitigation theory. Damages cannot be quantified on this record because the $275/sq ft figure has no stated square footage or comparator sale price attached to it.

issues.label: Breach of Right of First Refusal (liability)

outcome.description: After a bench trial the district court awarded the tenant $257,216 in damages plus post-judgment interest, using the tenant's damages methodology (unrealized appreciation, rent-versus-mortgage differential, lost principal) but valuing the unit at the $166.73 per square foot the third-party buyers paid rather than the $275 the tenant proposed. No attorney's fees. The Iowa Court of Appeals affirmed (2-1) on August 19, 2026, rejecting the estoppel-by-acquiescence and failure-to-mitigate defenses.
